body:
<!-- pr-reviewer: d1eb54692cf375bb7d7c7d818c83b93ec67d3629 -->
**Verdict: Needs changes before merge.** The probe hooks look sound, but #174 landed on main after this branch was cut. On current main every probe through the Haas, Mazak and Sinumerik posts is refused, and 8 of the 10 `probe_dialects` tests fail.

**What looks good**
- Haas and Mazak follow the Fanuc macro-B contract. G31 skip; trip read from #5061-#5063 in work coordinates; `#3000` alarms; `#5221 + 20 x slot + axis` and `G10 L2 P(n+1)` for the offset (Haas P2 = G55, correct).
- Mazak uses `IF[..]GOTO` with unique N labels (a test checks they are unique), the safer choice for older EIA generations.
- Sinumerik uses `MEAS=1 G1`, `$AC_MEA[1]`, `$AA_MW[axis]` (measured position in the workpiece coordinate system) and `SETAL`, plus `$P_UIFR[n,axis,TR]` with FI copied when the frame changes. This matches the documented 840D sl forms as far as I can judge without a controller. G58/G59 are refused by name, and only G54-G57 / G505-G599 are accepted.
- In all three posts the tolerance alarm comes before any offset write. The back-off is incremental (G91), the sign is folded into the operator, and units go through `fu`/`fw`.
- Heidenhain keeps a named refusal instead of a guessed TNC cycle, with a comment saying why. That is honest, but #173 is then 3 of 4 dialects.
- Only the three new `probe_bore_centre.nc` goldens are added. No existing golden changed, so cutting-op output is unchanged. Provenance comments cite public manuals, and the decision file is present.

**Local results** (merged with `upstream/main`, clean auto-merge; the PR touches no build.rs, .github, scripts or Cargo files)
- `probe_op` 11, `probe_guard` 5, `conformance` 6, `posting` 17, `probe_pick` 9, `probe_reach` 5, `inverted_probe` 8, `camcraft-post` suites: all pass.
- 24 other app suites that mention these dialects (cli, control_comp, drill_rplane, arc_planes, fanuc_post, heidenhain_*, inverted_*, sinumerik_safe_retract, and others): all pass.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `probe_dialects`: **2 passed, 8 failed**. The two that pass are the Sinumerik G59 refusal and the Heidenhain refusal.
```
probe_dialects.rs:75: ["probing: operation \"Probe1\": this post script does not define onProbeGuard - it cannot write a protected (stop-on-contact) positioning move, so the probe operation is refused"]
```

**Requested before merge**
1. Add `onProbeGuard()` to `assets/posts/haas.cps` (~line 460), `assets/posts/mazak.cps` (~line 461) and `assets/posts/sinumerik.cps` (~line 479), the #174 protected-move hook. Model it on `fanuc.cps:523-540`:
   - Haas: G31 plus a `#5061+` vs target test per moving axis, alarming `#3000=3(PROBE HIT ON POSITIONING)`.
   - Mazak: the same test in the `alarmUnless` GOTO form.
   - Sinumerik: a protected `MEAS=1 G1` plus a check that the move reached its target (`$AC_MEA[1]` / `$AA_MW[axis]` against the target), with `MSG` + `SETAL` + `M0`.
   Skip axes that hold still, as fanuc does.
2. Add a guard test per dialect (guard words present, alarm distinct from the no-contact one) and update the gate-map header.
3. Regenerate the three `probe_bore_centre.nc` goldens once the guard exists, and review the diff by eye. The committed ones predate the GUARD records.

**Notes (not blocking)**
- Heidenhain stays refused, so use `Refs #173` rather than `Fixes #173` unless a follow-up issue is filed for the TNC touch-probe cycles. The "stacked on #333" line in the body is stale: the diff is now only the 9 files.
- Mazak `#5061`/`#5221` numbering and the Sinumerik MEAS/`$AA_MW` path remain untested on a control or simulator, as the body says.
- Sinumerik refuses by name beyond 13 trips (R50..R88), which is good.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
